page: Amazon Web Services c3.xlarge is a legacy compute-optimized instance belonging to the third-generation C3 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 4 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing dedicated CPU allocation. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 1.88 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of an 80 GB NVMe SSD, and network performance is rated at a baseline of 1 Gbps. The virtualization is managed via the Xen hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate that the c3.xlarge sits in the lower performance tiers compared to modern cloud hardware. Its single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, consistently falls into the weak and poor categories. Memory bandwidth tests show read speeds of 26.21 GB/sec and write speeds of 22.34 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, which are also categorized as weak. The processor supports basic AVX and AES instructions but lacks newer vector extensions like AVX-512 or AMX.

Given its legacy hardware profile, the c3.xlarge offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring dedicated compute resources rather than shared-core burstable performance. However, the tradeoff is significantly reduced processing throughput and memory bandwidth compared to newer generations. It is best suited for legacy applications, basic web serving, lightweight batch processing, or development environments that benefit from dedicated vCPUs and local NVMe storage but do not demand high-performance computing.
